title: Batch-cache-tuner oscillation mitigation and assertive recovery playbook
creator: Alicia Morgan
description:
Summary: During a scheduled staged apply of new batching + KV cache recommendations from the Optimize autotuner, we observed repeated configuration oscillations that temporarily increased CPU/GPU utilization and client tail latency for several high-throughput tenants. This ticket captures the incident follow-up: a concise postmortem, immediate mitigations applied, and a playbook for assertive recovery and safer future applies.

Context: The autotuner proposed more aggressive prefix-caching and larger batch sizes for text-generation workloads based on simulated token distributions. The new config was applied to a canary cohort; telemetry showed transient improvement, but subsequent staged rollout triggered a cascading change in load shaping which caused the autoscaling and batching subsystems to repeatedly re-evaluate and flip configurations (oscillation). During oscillation, clients experienced 2–4x spike in p95/p99 latency and several request timeouts for ~12 minutes in aggregate across affected routes.
timeline:
2026-02-20 09:00 - Begin staged apply to canary cluster (10% traffic)
2026-02-20 09:06 - Observed lower mean token cost and slight latency improvement on canary
2026-02-20 09:12 - Canary autoscaler heuristics triggered due to bursty input load; batching pipeline recalculated target size
2026-02-20 09:15 - First rollback event triggered automatically by safety thresholds (throughput degradation signal)
2026-02-20 09:18 - Autotuner re-applied variant with different cache TTLs; configs started oscillating between variants every ~90s
2026-02-20 09:22 - P95/p99 latency increased in dedicated and shared pools; alerting fired
2026-02-20 09:26 - Ops throttled rollout and paused autotuner; manual mitigation started
2026-02-20 09:32 - Manual fixed config applied to canary; oscillation subsided; metrics back to baseline by 09:40
2026-02-20 09:45 - Post-incident mitigation plan drafted and initial runbook notes captured
root_cause: The autotuner did not sufficiently account for feedback loops between autoscaling heuristics and batching cache sizing when changing cache TTL + batch size simultaneously. Rapid staged rollouts combined with an autoscaler that reacts to short-lived bursts created a control-loop interaction that made the tuning engine flip choices based on transient signals. Additionally, safety thresholds were tuned to detect only throughput drops and not short tail-latency spikes, delaying automatic circuit-break activation.
mitigation_summary: Immediate steps: paused rollout, pinned stable config on affected clusters, and tightened the autotuner's minimum hold window (increased from 30s to 5m) to avoid re-evaluating on transient signals. Enabled a fast circuit-break rule to halt applies when p99 latency increases by more than 40% for 2 consecutive minutes. Added a temporary rate-limit for the autotuner apply traffic to reduce pressure on autoscalers.
immediate_actions: Paused all staged applies from Optimize autotuner and switched to manual approval for the next 48h
Pinned last-known-good batching/cache config in canary and promoted the same to remaining clusters until validation completes
Raised circuit-break sensitivity: p99 latency delta threshold -> 40% over 2m, and add fallback to conservative config
Added a 1-minute debounce on autoscaler triggers for canary groups to reduce reaction to microbursts
Notified Customer Success and affected tenants; offered monitoring window and support for impacted routes
long_term_actions: Model the control-loop: build a simulation harness that runs autoscaler + batching + autotuner together on synthetic burst traces
Split tuning dimensions: avoid simultaneous large changes to cache TTL and batch sizing in a single apply; introduce sequential phased changes with validation gates
Enhance safety checks: add tail-latency-based stop conditions and require sustained improvement for >= 3 sampling windows before promoting
Introduce a staged-apply quorum: require both telemetry and a shadow A/B run showing stable tail-latency before rollout to next cohort
Ship a canary-allocator: run new configs in a resource-isolated canary pool to avoid perturbing global autoscaler signals
rollback_steps: Trigger manual rollback via deployment console: select affected cluster -> revert to last-known-good config UUID
If revert fails: enable conservative global fallback (runtime flag): optimize.force_conservative=true
Reconcile autotuner state: mark current proposal as suppressed for 24h and annotate rationale
After rollback, run validation suite: smoke-gen load test + tail-latency checks for 10 minutes before unpausing rollout
validation_plan: Validation gating for future applies: 1) Shadow run for 30 minutes on 5% traffic with telemetry capture. 2) Run synthetic burst tests using the new simulation harness to ensure no oscillatory response across three independent runs. 3) Require p95/p99 latency to be <= 10% above baseline and throughput to be >= baseline before canary promotion. 4) Post-promotion monitor window: 60 minutes with auto-rollback on any 30s window crossing safety thresholds.
postmortem_notes:
Lessons learned: autotuner must treat autoscaling as part of its environment—not an independent metric. Short feedback windows led to overfitting to transient patterns. The safety gating prioritized throughput/throughput-cost but underweighted tail-latency, which drove user-visible degradation.

Decision log: we scoped three immediate config changes (hold window increase, circuit-break thresholds, debounce on autoscaler). We prioritized minimal blast radius and fast recoverability. The team agreed to delay aggressive cost-saving recommendations until the control-loop simulator and enhanced validation pipeline are in place.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Simulation harness exists and reproduces oscillation for at least 2 historical traces. 2) New staged-apply process prevents re-evaluation for at least 5 minutes after an apply. 3) Safety gates triggered by tail-latency work end-to-end and auto-pause applies on threshold breaches. 4) Post-apply monitoring dashboard and alerting are updated with clear runbook links and on-call rotation notes.
notes: Communicated to customer success and SRE on 2026-02-20; suggested customers may see short-lived latencies during the incident window. We will publish an incident summary to tenants by 2026-03-12 after internal review.
final_resolution: Temporary mitigations applied and rollout paused. Ownership assigned for simulation harness, staged-apply protocol, and safety gate enhancements. Targeting full remediation and new validation pipeline in optimize-2.5 release cycle.
